entries.textEn:
Fault Symptom | Troubleshooting Method | Cause Investigation | Replacement Part | Test Equipment
DC input fault | Charge the power station with a DC adjustable power supply and observe the output power of the DC adjustable power supply | Check whether the power station's DC input port is loose or damaged; use a multimeter to check for voltage output across the positive and negative terminals of the DC adapter board
Check the charging board for output voltage; if there is no output, substitute the charging board to troubleshoot
Check whether the voltage across the battery positive and negative terminals on the battery protection board is normal; if normal, test whether the voltages at the battery protection board's input and output terminals are normal; if abnormal, substitute the battery protection board to troubleshoot | Charging connector | DC adjustable power supply
Multimeter
 | Charging board | Replace the charging board | Charging board | 
 | Battery protection board | Replace the battery protection board | Battery protection board | 
 | Solar panel | Use a multimeter to check whether the solar panel output voltage is normal
Connect the test equipment and test for power output | Solar panel | Multimeter
Power station
AC input fault | Connect an AC tester to charge the power station and observe the output power on the AC tester | Use a multimeter to test the AC cable returned by the user and confirm whether AC is normal | AC cable | AC tester
Multimeter
 | Three-pin input connector | Check whether the power station's AC input port is loose or damaged; use a multimeter to check for voltage output at the rear of the three-pin connector | Three-pin input connector | 
 | Overcurrent protector | Check whether the AC input overcurrent protector plug is connected properly; use the multimeter's continuity buzzer mode to check whether the overcurrent protector is OK | Overcurrent protector | 
 | Bidirectional inverter | With no AC input connected, activate the AC control button and check whether AC output is normal; if the output is abnormal, substitute the bidirectional inverter to verify the issue | Bidirectional inverter | 
 | Battery protection board | Check whether the voltage across the battery positive and negative terminals on the battery protection board is normal; if normal, test whether the voltages at the battery protection board's input and output terminals are normal; if abnormal, substitute the battery protection board to troubleshoot | Battery protection board | 
Battery cannot be fully charged | Reset the power station's system | Press and hold the display button and USB control button to reset; check whether resetting the system resolves the issue | System error | 
 |  | Check whether the voltage across the battery positive and negative terminals on the battery protection board is normal; if normal, test whether the battery protection board's output voltage is normal; if abnormal, substitute the battery protection board to troubleshoot | Battery protection board damaged | Multimeter
 |  | Measure the voltage of an individual cell group to check whether it is within the standard range, | Battery pack | Multimeter

entries.textEn:
Fault Symptom | Troubleshooting Method | Cause Investigation | Replacement Part | Test Equipment
AC cannot be activated | Confirm whether the product has sufficient battery charge | Insufficient battery charge; recharge the product | Recharge | 
 |  | Battery charge is normal, but AC cannot be activated; test whether AC control is OK; if faulty, replace the mainboard; if OK, substitute | Inverter | 
 |  | Battery charge is normal, but AC cannot be activated; test whether AC control is OK; if faulty, replace the mainboard; if OK, substitute | Mainboard | 
 |  | Check whether the voltage across the battery positive and negative terminals on the battery protection board is normal; if normal, test whether the battery protection board's output voltage is normal; if abnormal, substitute the battery protection board to troubleshoot | Battery protection board | 
AC can be activated, but there is no output | Turn on the USB/DC/AC switches | Adjust the AC load to the power station's maximum output power (refer to the specification label on the unit) to perform a verification test | Equipment power is too high; product output protection | AC load
 |  | Visually inspect the AC socket for abnormalities and use a multimeter to verify | AC socket | Multimeter
 |  | USB output tests normal, but AC has no output; substitute the inverter for verification testing | Inverter | 
 |  | Neither USB nor AC has output, indicating a faulty mainboard; substitute the mainboard for verification testing | Mainboard | 
AC output shuts off automatically during discharge | Turn on AC and discharge with an AC load | Equipment power is too high; product self-protection | Output power exceeded | AC load
 |  | USB charging and discharging functions are normal; only AC output shuts off automatically | Inverter | AC load
